So yeah, this is the empire that Braverman wants to praise

Births were strikingly low, and with almost no schools on the estates, children joined weeding gangs at ten and were indentured as soon as the law allowed. Over all of this lay the penal system, which made breaking a contract a crime and required the indentured to carry a livret (a pass)...

Medical care was minimal. A 1902 report found fifteen doctors for an estate population of 91,924, three of them responsible for 11,000 people each. Family life was distorted by how few women were there: as late as 1873 there were only about forty for every hundred men on the estates...

New arrivals, often ill and distressed after the voyage, were given no time to adjust. They went straight onto task work, where an unfinished task meant no pay at all. The planters’ most powerful way of avoiding wages was the “double cut”: a day’s absence for any reason cost two days’ pay...

I went to Mauritius to look at what happened during indenture period for Empireworld. Labourers might start at 4 am, moving boulders in punishing heat, and were used for ploughing and hauling, work better suited to animals. Women got up at 3.30 to cook for families before doing the same labour...
